title: Move more water aside
hook: Change submerged volume and predict buoyant force.
misconception: buoyant force stays fixed when submerged volume doubles.
objective: Apply F_b = ρgV to compare buoyant force when submerged volume changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a body immersed in the same fluid under fixed gravity, F_b = ρgV. When submerged volume doubles, buoyant force becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F_b = ρgV; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a body immersed in the same fluid under fixed gravity, with a nonzero initial result. If submerged volume triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on buoyant force?
recall.why: Apply F_b = ρgV under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
